text:
maria: Heads-up — bringing up the new hf/model-x on Redwood convert pipeline and ran into a weird failure during safetensors shard merge. Splits look fine but final merge fails with key mismatch errors and then the revpin logic falls back to master and pulls a different shard set.

sam: Ugh. Can you paste the error? sounds like weight key rename + shard index inconsistency.

maria: Sure — root error snippet:
```
Traceback: KeyError: 'model.layers.12.attn.q_proj.weight' while merging shard 3/5
During revpin fallback: downloaded revision "main" instead of "rev-2026-03-19" due to auth cache returning 401->retry->anon
```

alex: Two things to check: 1) convert tool's weightname mapping (we had a rename rule for q_proj->query_proj lingering) 2) hub downloader auth cache TTL bug that can return a stale 401 and then downloader falls back to unauthenticated mirror (different snapshot).

maria: I grepped the mapping and found an entry in converters/legacy_map.json that maps "q_proj"->"query_proj" but the new model uses "q_proj" in some shards and "query_proj" in others — looks like the convert step normalized some files but not others.

leo: If shards were produced at different times (revpin mismatch), weightnames can differ. How did you trigger revpin fallback? was there a 403/401?

maria: Yes, the hub request for shard 2 returned 401 (token expired). The downloader retried unauthenticated and got a cached CDN snapshot which was missing the renamed keys. The convert pipeline then attempted to merge and KeyError.

jen: This is why we added a strict revpin check in the safer import path. But I remember a recent PR that relaxed retry behavior for faster cold downloads — might've introduced the auth cache race.

sam: Repro steps? can we trigger locally with HUB_TOKEN expired and see deterministic failure?

maria: Repro script I ran:
```bash
export HF_TOKEN=old_token
python convert.py --model hf/model-x --out redwood-format --force-shard-merge
# then simulate token refresh delay so downloader sees 401 then anon
```
It fails ~95% on my laptop with that pattern.

alex: Ok we should: 1) patch downloader to never fallback to unauthenticated on revpin requests (explicitly require auth for revpin pins) 2) make converter tolerant: detect weightname canonicalization mismatch and emit mapping report before merge 3) add a sanity check step to compare per-shard key sets and abort with clear message instead of crashing.

leo: Also add a small CLI flag --strict-revpin that enforces exact revision matching and fails early if token is not valid. That will help CI.

jen: I'll own the downloader fix (auth-cache TTL + no-unauth-fallback for revpin). alex can you own the mapping report? sam can add unit test harness for shard key diffs?

alex: Yep will add a pre-merge hook that prints a diff of weight names and suggests common renames. Example output: 
```
Shard 1 missing: query_proj.weight
Shard 3 has: q_proj.weight
Suggested mapping: q_proj -> query_proj (apply with --apply-rename-map)
```

sam: I'll write tests that simulate 401->anon fallback and assert we error out and don't silently use mismatched shards.

maria: Thanks all. For now I reran convert with explicit env to force auth refresh and it succeeded once I ensured the same revision across all shards. But this will bite customers.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: converter-auth-fix (jen) -> staging at 2026-03-21T02:00Z

deploy-bot: canary rollout initiated: converters v1.23.4 -> 10%

maria: tagging the model onboarding ticket with the repro steps and adding the shard-diff output to the thread. Will follow up if flaky after the canary.
